Problem: For which integer values of $p$ and $q$ will the equation $x^{2} + p x + q = 0$ have one root that is 4 times the other? How many solutions do we get if we consider $p$ and $q$ to have at most two digits?

<reflection>
The roots can be written as $r$ and $4r$. Vieta's formulas give $p = -5r$ and $q = 4r^2$. For at most two digits, $|p| \le 99$ and $|q| \le 99$. From $|p| \le 99$, the bound is $|r| \le 19.8$, so the listed integer candidate set is $\{-19,-18,\ldots,18,19\}$.
The count is wrong: the integers from -19 to 19 inclusive contain 19 negative integers, 19 positive integers, and 0, totaling 39, not 21.
Recount the candidate integers from -19 to 19 correctly as 39, then impose the remaining two-digit restriction on $q$.
</reflection>
